text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub wrote to U.S. Secretary of State Madeline Albright warned that the reported deployment of Prithvi missiles by India near the Pakistan border had created a dangerous security environment combined with the potential to unleash a missile race in South Asia.
- A 50-megawatt multi-purpose nuclear power reactor made by Pakistani engineers has started working near Khushab.

- The government has decided to withdraw the Letter of Support issued to Gordon Wu's company Consolidate Electric Power of Asia to set up a coal-fired power plant and a port with an estimated cost of $1.0 billion at Keti Bander.
- The 1997/98 (July-June) budget will be presented in the National Assembly on June 13 instead of June 14.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has offered a scheme to 8,100 loan defaulters under which they can clear defaults of more than 127 billion rupees with state-run banks and institutions.
- The central bank has designed a three-pronged strategy to help banks lend at cheaper rates and pay higher returns on deposits.
- The Privatisation Commission has invited applications for the appointment of financial advisors for the state-run Investment Corporation of Pakistan.
- The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources will undergo a complete restructuring.
- The first locally manufactured airframes of K-8 jet trainers were formally handed to China at the Pakistan Aeronautical Complex in Kamra.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Privatisation Commission has offered 10 public sector cooking oil manufacturing units for an open auction.
- The central bank warned bank defaulters that the legal system had been changed and a comprehensive law was in place to deal with the recovery of non-performing loans.
FINANCIAL POST
- Standard Chartered Group has agreed to sell its share holdings in the Standard Chartered Mercantile Leasing Co to Saudi Pak Industrial and Agricultral Investment Co.
THE NEWS
- Pakistan told the United States that the threat posed by India's reported deploymnet of Prithvi missiles has left Islamabad with no option but to take appropriate counter-measures.
THE NATION
- Chief Ehtesab Commissioner Ghulam Mujadid Mirza denied any difference with the government on the new accountability law.
THE FRONTIER POST
- World Tel, a leading name in the international communication world is exploring the possibilities to invest $200 million in Pakistan's telecom sector.
-- Islamabad newsroom 274757
